Snowflake

Source: vignettes/snowflake.Rmd
snowflake.Rmd

Snowflake is a hosted SQL data platform. A warehouse supplies the compute for queries, while a role determines which data a user can access. A Shiny app can use each visitor’s Snowflake account and role to apply those same permissions.

oauth_db_snowflake() provides a DBI connection for SQL or dbplyr. The first example shows the signed-in user’s name and role so you can check the connection before querying your tables.

Try the guided demo

Run shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_cloud_demo("snowflake") in the R console for an editable app. It walks through your account, role, warehouse and OAuth registration. Install odbc, bslib, processx, askpass and the Snowflake ODBC driver first.

Sign in, then click Run example query. Queries may resume a warehouse and consume credits; stopping the local app doesn’t suspend the warehouse. See Getting started for editing and ?oauth_db_cloud_demo for optional settings.

Snowflake setup

In R, run install.packages("odbc"), then install the Snowflake ODBC driver for your operating system. Ask your administrator for a custom-client OAuth integration with http://localhost:8100 as its redirect URI. Users need a role with access to the warehouse and data.

For this local HTTP callback, the development integration needs OAUTH_ALLOW_NON_TLS_REDIRECT_URI = TRUE. Use an HTTPS callback when deploying. The integration settings describe this option and refresh-token settings.

Save the integration’s client ID and secret in a local .Renviron file, then restart R:

OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
Setting Where to get it
server Your account’s connection details; use its .snowflakecomputing.com hostname
warehouse, database, role Names your Snowflake administrator grants to the users
Client ID and secret The custom-client security integration, shown below

If the integration doesn’t exist yet, follow Create the OAuth integration after the app example.

A complete app

Save this as example.R. Replace the connection settings, keeping the server and role the same in the sign-in client and connection helper:

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_snowflake_client(
  server = "organization-account.snowflakecomputing.com",
  role = "REPORTING_READER",
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_snowflake(
    auth$connection,
    server = "organization-account.snowflakecomputing.com",
    role = "REPORTING_READER",
    warehouse = "REPORTING_WH",
    database = "ANALYTICS"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER(), CURRENT_ROLE()")
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at http://localhost:8100
# (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. cannot perform necessary redirects)

Run source("example.R") and open http://localhost:8100. Sign in to run the query; signing out clears the output.

Query a table

Replace the output expression with SQL for your data. For example, if your table is ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS:

output$rows <- renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT * FROM ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS LIMIT 20")
})

con() gets the current user’s connection. Call it inside the render or reactive expression before using DBI or dbplyr.

Create the OAuth integration

A Snowflake administrator can run this in a SQL worksheet to register a local development app:

CREATE SECURITY INTEGRATION shiny_reporting
  TYPE = OAUTH
  ENABLED = TRUE
  OAUTH_CLIENT = CUSTOM
  OAUTH_CLIENT_TYPE = 'CONFIDENTIAL'
  OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI = 'http://localhost:8100'
  OAUTH_ALLOW_NON_TLS_REDIRECT_URI = TRUE
  OAUTH_ENFORCE_PKCE = TRUE
  OAUTH_ISSUE_REFRESH_TOKENS = TRUE;

SELECT SYSTEM$SHOW_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRETS('SHINY_REPORTING');

Copy OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET into .Renviron as OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID and OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET. The integration registers the app; grant users the reporting role and that role’s warehouse/table permissions separately. Use HTTPS and disable the non-TLS redirect exception when deploying. Snowflake’s custom-client guide covers integration privileges and role restrictions.

Connection defaults

Set schema = "PUBLIC" on the helper to choose a default schema. Omit warehouse, database, or schema to use the account’s defaults. If the installed ODBC driver has a different name, set driver. See ?oauth_db_snowflake for the full arguments.

External OAuth

If Snowflake uses Entra, Okta, or another external provider for OAuth, configure a shinyOAuth client for that provider. Request the audience and role scopes accepted by your Snowflake integration.

Connect with oauth_db_snowflake() as above. Set target if your client uses named token targets, and required_scopes to the integration’s role scope. For native Snowflake OAuth, the helper derives that scope from role; external providers may use different scope names. Getting started explains custom targets.
